newsitem.title: USA: Small fire at Cardon refinery unit cuts alkylation.
newsitem.headline: Small fire at Cardon refinery unit cuts alkylation.

text.p: A unit of Maraven's Cardon refinery was hit by a small fire Thursday morning, causing the company to cut processing at its alkylation unit by around 50 percent or some 6,000 barrels per day (bpd), a company official said on Friday.
The fire at the plant's olefins treatment unit took place at around the same time that the 305,000 bpd refinery was returning to full operation after a total power outage last Sunday night.
The official said the fire was caused by a "small leak," and that the 12,000 bpd alkylation unit would be running at a reduced rate for about a week.

The alkylation unit, which produces gasoline blendstocks, should begin to increase its processing shortly once olefins begin arriving from Lagoven's Amuay refinery, which is connected to Cardon by pipeline, the official said.
"Customers won't be affected," the official said, referring to the possibility of alternative supplies from Amuay and the affiliated Isla refinery in Curacao.
Maraven and Lagoven are operating subsidiaries of state Petroleos de Venezuela.
